## The question

[How to elegantly create a pyramid hierarchy in tikz](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/110522/how-to-elegantly-create-a-pyramid-hierarchy-in-tikz), asked by [Elpezmuerto](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/736/elpezmuerto) on TeX Stack Exchange (2013-04-24; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I want to create a pyramid hierarchy in tikz with smooth sides (unlike [this step-pyramid][q-1]) and place text in each level. Shown below is how I am currently doing this, is there a better way?
>
> ```latex
> \documentclass{article}
> \usepackage{tikz}
> \begin{document}
> \begin{figure}[!h]
> \centering
> \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.73]
>
> \def \h {9};
> \def \f {.7};
>
> \foreach \y in  {0,1,2,3,4,5,6} {
> 	\def \w { \h*\f-\y*\f };
> 	\def \v { \y*\f-\h*\f };
> 	\draw (\v,\y) -- (\w,\y);
> }
>
> \draw (-\h*\f,0)  -- (0,\h);
> \draw (\h*\f,0)  -- (0,\h);
>
> \node at (0,0) [above] {G};
> \node at (0,1) [above] {F};
> \node at (0,2) [above] {E};
> \node at (0,3) [above] {D};
> \node at (0,4) [above] {C};
> \node at (0,5) [above] {B};
> \node at (0,6) [above] {A};
> \end{tikzpicture}
> \end{figure}
> \end{document}
> ```
>
> ![enter image description here][q-2]
>
>
>   [q-1]: https://tex.stackexchange.com/q/54343/736

Here is a simplification using the tikz intersections library to cut down on brute-force calculation:

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{tikz}
\usetikzlibrary{intersections}
\begin{document}

\begin{tikzpicture}
\coordinate (A) at (-5,0);
\coordinate (B) at ( 5,0);
\coordinate (C) at (0,7);
\draw[name path=AC] (A) -- (C);
\draw[name path=BC] (B) -- (C);
\foreach \y/\A in {0/G,1/F,2/E,3/D,4/C,5/B,6/A} {
	\path[name path=horiz] (A|-0,\y) -- (B|-0,\y);
	\draw[name intersections={of=AC and horiz,by=P},
	      name intersections={of=BC and horiz,by=Q}] (P) -- (Q)
		node[midway,above] {\A};
}
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{document}
```

Notice the combination of level numbers and labels as in Gonzalo's comment.

![sample code output][1]

Here is another solution using the tikz calculations library:

```latex
\foreach \y/\A in {0/G,1/F,2/E,3/D,4/C,5/B,6/A} {
	\draw ($(A)!\y/7!(C)$) -- ($(B)!\y/7!(C)$)
        node[midway,above] {\A};
}
```

The coordinate `($(A)!\y/7!(C)$)` is `\y/7` of the way between the coordinates `A` and `C`.  The advantage here is total DRY: Change any of the coordinates `A`, `B`, or `C`, and the pyramid will transform accordingly.

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{tikz}
\usetikzlibrary{calc}
\begin{document}

\begin{tikzpicture}
\coordinate (A) at (-5,0);
\coordinate (B) at ( 5,1);
\coordinate (C) at (0,3);
\draw (A) -- (C);
\draw (B) -- (C);
\foreach \y/\A in {0/G,1/F,2/E,3/D,4/C,5/B,6/A} {
	\draw ($(A)!\y/7!(C)$) -- ($(B)!\y/7!(C)$) node[midway,above] {\A};
}
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{document}
```

![sample code output][2]

**Edit 2024-11-08**: To celebrate a few more upvotes 11 years after my original answer, I found a way to streamline the code further:

* Using the `count` key to `\foreach`, the list index doesn't need to be hard-coded.
* There's no way to count the number of levels without iterating it over it twice, but by making the list of levels a macro, we can do that once to count, then to draw.
* We store the number of levels in a counter, which allows us to use the same name as the list of levels itself (internally it becomes a different control sequence).

So now it looks like:

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{tikz}
\usetikzlibrary{calc}
\begin{document}

\begin{tikzpicture}

% Define vertices and levels
\coordinate (A) at (-5,0);
\coordinate (B) at ( 5,1);
\coordinate (C) at (0,3);
\newcommand{\levels}{G,F,E,D,C,B,A}

\draw (A) -- (C);
\draw (B) -- (C);

% count the number of levels
\newcounter{levels}
\foreach \A in \levels {\stepcounter{levels}}

\foreach[count=\y from 0] \A in \levels {
    \draw ($(A)!\y/\the\value{levels}!(C)$) 
        -- ($(B)!\y/\the\value{levels}!(C)$) 
        node[midway,above] {\A};
}
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{document}
```
